intro: Interior designers coordinate clients, contractors and details, skills that architecture and design careers share. The closest of the 25 careers below is Landscape Architects, with an 83% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $79,870, which is 19% more than the $67,190 interior designers earn.
why_it_works: A project means understanding how a client lives or works, planning space and materials and keeping trades on schedule. O*NET rates coordination, service orientation and social perceptiveness at 3.75 out of 5 for this job. Architecture, drafting and set design use the same visual and planning skills. Almost all matches need no new degree. The gaps are quality checks and systems evaluation.
tips: Architects earn $99,280, which is 48% more, but usually need a graduate degree and license.
Theatrical makeup artists earn $97,150, or 45% more, if you are drawn to stage and film work.
Purchasing Managers earn $148,080 and value your supplier and material knowledge.

faq.q: What jobs can former interior designers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Landscape Architects (83%), architectural and civil drafters (77%) and architects (72%), based on O*NET 31.0. Film and Video Editors are 67% matched and earn $75,420, which is 12% more than the $67,190 interior designer median.

faq.q: Which careers for interior designers pay more?
faq.a: 16 of the 25 matches pay more. Marketing Managers earn $166,790 (148% more), Purchasing Managers $148,080 (120% more) and Advertising and Promotions Managers $133,660 (99% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Manager roles usually expect business experience.

faq.q: Do interior designers need another degree?
faq.a: Rarely. 24 of the 25 matches need no more education than interior designers already have, and only architecture usually needs a graduate degree. A bachelor's degree is common, held by 85% of workers in the closest match, so a design portfolio is what most employers look at first.

faq.q: What skills should interior designers learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are quality control analysis, systems evaluation, equipment selection and operations analysis. Complex problem solving already rates 3.62 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so technical drawing and building systems are the main steps for most moves.
